question: Your team uses Claude Code on a large React codebase. Test files named *.test.tsx sit beside their components in dozens of feature directories, and new directories are added every sprint. You want the team's testing conventions to load whenever Claude Code edits any test file, wherever it lives, while staying out of context for other files. Which configuration best meets this goal?

options.text: Create a .claude/rules/ file whose YAML frontmatter sets paths: ["**/*.test.tsx"], so the testing conventions load when Claude Code edits any test file.
options.reason: A glob pattern in the paths field matches files by type regardless of directory location, and the rule loads only when Claude Code edits matching files.

options.text: Create a .claude/rules/ file whose YAML frontmatter sets paths: ["src/components/*.test.tsx"], so the testing conventions load for component test files.
options.reason: This glob is tied to one directory, so test files in other feature directories are missed; the conventions must apply by file type regardless of directory.

options.text: Copy the testing conventions into a CLAUDE.md file inside each feature directory that currently contains test files.
options.reason: Directory-level CLAUDE.md files are bound to directories, so they suit conventions spanning many directories poorly; glob-pattern rules are preferred for files spread across the codebase.

options.text: Add the testing conventions to the root project CLAUDE.md file so they are available during every editing task.
options.reason: The conventions would load for every file, which adds irrelevant context and token usage that path-scoped rules avoid.
